note: Core requirement catalogue for assessing a cross-border transfer of health data. It names the questions and why each one gates the transfer or is advisory; it never states the answer. Keys are stable and are used by findings, records and attestations. 'gate' = must be met (or attested) before the transfer; 'advisory' = ongoing duty, reported but not blocking. The first item of each regime is its applicability gate: if it is not applicable, the rest of that regime is not assessed.

evidence_types.executed_agreement: A signed agreement, e.g. SCCs, a processor contract, a BAA or a data use agreement
evidence_types.certification_record: A certification or listing, e.g. an entry on the Data Privacy Framework list
evidence_types.approval_record: An approval or declaration, e.g. ethics approval, IRB waiver documentation, a Committee declaration
evidence_types.consent_record: Records of consent or authorization obtained from the individuals
evidence_types.legal_basis_record: A documented legal basis, e.g. the statutory function relied on
evidence_types.role_determination: A documented determination of a party's role or regulated status
evidence_types.assessment_document: A completed assessment, e.g. DPIA, transfer impact assessment, anonymisation or de-identification determination
evidence_types.data_specification: The exact fields, identifiers and volume of data to be transferred
evidence_types.policy_or_procedure: A policy or procedure that is in force, e.g. minimum-necessary or security procedures
evidence_types.attestation_statement: A signed statement by a responsible person that a stated fact is true

requirements.title: GDPR applies to this processing
requirements.question: Does the GDPR apply: material and territorial scope, and are the data personal data (including pseudonymised data) rather than anonymous?
requirements.class_reason: Every other GDPR requirement depends on it (Arts. 2-3; personal data, Art. 4(1) and Recital 26).

requirements.title: Arrangements required by the parties' roles
requirements.question: What are the parties' roles (controller, joint controller, processor) and are the arrangements those roles require in place (Art. 26 arrangement or Art. 28 contract)?
requirements.class_reason: Processing by a processor must be governed by a contract (Art. 28(3)); joint controllers must have an arrangement (Art. 26(1)).

requirements.title: Lawful basis (Art. 6)
requirements.question: Which Article 6(1) basis covers the sender's disclosure and the recipient's processing, including any further processing, and does it hold on the stated facts?
requirements.class_reason: Processing is lawful only if and to the extent that at least one Art. 6(1) basis applies.

requirements.title: Condition for health or genetic data (Art. 9)
requirements.question: Which Article 9(2) condition permits processing the health or genetic data, and is it met on the stated facts?
requirements.class_reason: Art. 9(1) prohibits processing health and genetic data unless an Art. 9(2) condition applies.

requirements.title: Transfer mechanism (Chapter V)
requirements.question: Is there a transfer to a third country, and if so which Chapter V mechanism (adequacy, appropriate safeguards, derogation) covers it?
requirements.class_reason: Art. 44: a transfer may take place only if the conditions in Chapter V are complied with.

requirements.title: Safeguards for research processing (Art. 89(1))
requirements.question: If the processing is for scientific research or statistics, are the Art. 89(1) safeguards in place (data minimisation, pseudonymisation where possible)?
requirements.class_reason: Research processing under Art. 9(2)(j) must be in accordance with Art. 89(1).

requirements.title: Data minimisation for the stated purpose (Art. 5(1)(c))
requirements.question: Are the data to be transferred adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the stated purpose? Relate each described data category, the identifiability level, the number of people and who can access the data to that purpose, and name any element that exceeds it or could be reduced (for example by pseudonymised or less detailed data) without defeating the purpose.
requirements.class_reason: Art. 5(1)(c) governs the data sent in this transfer itself; data beyond what the purpose needs may not be transferred, so excess data must be removed before the transfer.

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment (Art. 35)
requirements.question: Is the processing likely to result in a high risk (for example large-scale health or genetic data), and if so has a DPIA been carried out before the processing?
requirements.class_reason: Art. 35(1): carried out prior to processing likely to result in a high risk; Art. 35(3)(b) lists large-scale special-category processing.

requirements.title: Security of processing (Art. 32)
requirements.question: Are appropriate technical and organisational security measures described for the transfer and the recipient's processing?
requirements.class_reason: Art. 32 is an ongoing duty of controller and processor; it does not by itself decide whether this transfer may take place.

requirements.title: Transparency, records, rights and retention
requirements.question: Are the ongoing duties covered: information to data subjects (Arts. 13-14), records of processing (Art. 30), data-subject rights and retention limits?
requirements.class_reason: Ongoing accountability duties (Art. 5(2)); they apply alongside the transfer rather than gating it.

requirements.title: HIPAA applies to this disclosure
requirements.question: Is the sender or recipient a covered entity or business associate, and is the information protected health information (rather than de-identified)?
requirements.class_reason: HIPAA's rules apply only to covered entities and business associates and to protected health information (45 CFR 160.102, 164.500; 164.514(a)).

requirements.title: Disclosure is permitted
requirements.question: On what basis is the use or disclosure permitted (treatment, payment or operations; authorization; research waiver; limited data set; another permission), and is it met?
requirements.class_reason: A covered entity or business associate may not use or disclose PHI except as permitted or required (45 CFR 164.502(a)).

requirements.title: Required agreements (BAA, data use agreement)
requirements.question: Does the disclosure require a business associate agreement or a data use agreement, and is it in place?
requirements.class_reason: Disclosure to a business associate needs satisfactory assurances in a contract (164.502(e), 164.504(e)); a limited data set needs a data use agreement (164.514(e)(4)).

requirements.title: Minimum necessary
requirements.question: Is the disclosure limited to the minimum necessary for its purpose, or does an exception apply?
requirements.class_reason: Uses and disclosures must be limited to the minimum necessary (164.502(b)), subject to listed exceptions.

requirements.title: Security Rule safeguards
requirements.question: Are administrative and technical safeguards in place for electronic PHI in transit and at rest?
requirements.class_reason: Security Rule safeguards (164.308, 164.312) are ongoing duties of the regulated entity.

requirements.title: Obligations of a regulated recipient
requirements.question: If the recipient is itself a covered entity or business associate, what duties apply to it once it holds the information?
requirements.class_reason: These apply to the recipient after receipt; they do not decide whether the sender may disclose.
